[EVENT] User is planning to try a yin yoga class this week.  
[PREFERENCE] User has been doing Vinyasa flow classes and really enjoys them.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking forward to trying something new with yin yoga.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Yin yoga is a slower-paced, meditative practice that targets deeper tissues of the body, such as connective tissues, joints, and bones.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Benefits of yin yoga include deep relaxation, increased flexibility, improved joint health, emotional balance, and mindfulness.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Yin yoga differs from Vinyasa flow in pace, focus, postures, breath, and sequence.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for a yin yoga beginner include arriving early, dressing comfortably, being prepared to slow down, listening to the body, focusing on breath, not comparing oneself to others, communicating with the teacher, being patient, staying hydrated, and having fun.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In a yin yoga class, one can expect a slow-paced practice with long holds (typically 3-5 minutes), a focus on deep breathing, targeted postures, a calm atmosphere, and guidance from the teacher.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User asked for recommendations for good yin yoga classes or teachers in their area.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested searching "yin yoga classes near me" or "yin yoga [user's city/state]" for local studios and classes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended checking local yoga studio websites for yin yoga offerings and looking for studios that specialize in yin yoga or have experienced teachers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant mentioned using yoga apps like YogaGlo, DoYouYoga, or Yoga International to find yin yoga classes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested asking friends, family, or fellow yoga practitioners for recommendations.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant advised looking for yoga associations for additional resources.
